### `Text`  <sub>type alias</sub>

```
type Text = List Char
```

`command.ges` declares this too, and for the same reason: it is not
in the core prelude and a file that wants strings has to say so.


## A field


### `Value`  <sub>data</sub>

```
Value := Word | Number | Names
```

What a field's value is written as.  Every value in this format is
one whitespace-free token (`notes.py`, F203), so this says how to
read that token and nothing about layout.

`Names` is the comma-separated list `voices melody,upper,bass`
already writes — one token still, and the only shape beyond a word
and a number that the two formats in the tree use.


### `Need`  <sub>data</sub>

```
Need := Must | May
```

Whether a record of this kind has to carry the field.  The refusal a
missing one earns names it, so this is what makes that message
derivable rather than written twice.


### `Field`  <sub>data</sub>

```
Field := Field Text Value Need
```


## A kind


### `Shape`  <sub>data</sub>

```
Shape := Named | Bare Text | Headed Text
```

What the tokens after the kind word are.

`Named` — `key value key value …`, and nothing positional, which is
gate two of `spec/drawnscores.md`: *two fields of one shape telling
apart only by position* is the failure that made `manner`
unfindable.  `note` is this.

`Bare` — one value and no name, under the field name given.  `bpm 96`
is this, and so is every singleton line of a `.desk`.

`Headed` — one bare value first, then named fields.  `section A  key
D  bars 8` is this, and the bare one is the record's own name.


### `Sort`  <sub>data</sub>

```
Sort := By Text | Along Text Text Text | Among Text Text
```

How the lines of a kind are sorted when the file is written back.

`By` is the ordinary case: this field, ascending.

`Along` is the one the roll forced — the voice order is *the
section's own*, not alphabetical, because that is the order the roll
stacks them in (Henri, 2026-09-05).  So it names the field, the kind
that writes the order down, and that kind's field holding it.

`Among` is where a reference is ordered by **where the record it
names stands**: a note's `section` sorts by the section's place in
the file and not by its name, because a section is put where the
author put it.  Found 2026-09-09 by deriving the writer from this
declaration and noticing that `By "section"` agreed with the parser
only because `arc.notes` happens to name its sections A, B, C.


### `Kind`  <sub>data</sub>

```
Kind := Kind Text Shape (List Field) (List Text) (List Sort)
```

One kind of fact: its word, the shape of its line, its fields, the
fields that are its **key**, and the order its lines are written in.

**An empty key means at most one record of this kind in a
document** — `bpm` is declared twice is a refusal, not a second fact.
**An empty order means the order they were written in**, which is
what `section` has: a section list is the author's sequence and
sorting it would be a second thing to be canonical about.
